items.title: Chicago pays the nation's highest price to remove lead water lines
items.summary: Chicago pays two to three times what nearby suburbs pay to remove toxic lead water lines, about $33,784 per line compared with $10,950 in Elgin, according to Axios Chicago. At that rate the city faces roughly $13.5 billion to replace its 400,000 lead lines over two decades, a cost that will fall heavily on taxpayers. City officials have not identified concrete plans to lower the charges, even as a federal rule will require removing 20,000 lines a year.
